sources.title: Yuri Koryakov, Linguistic Geography of Tundra Nenets: the History of the Western Groups
sources.note: International Journal of Eurasian Linguistics 7 article checked at journal pages 119 to 120 for early evidence, the 1545 charter, and its printed “Stephen Barrow” 1556 notice; page 121 for late sixteenth-century western Tundra Nenets distribution; and page 122 for the fuller charter text.

sources.title: Dartmouth Libraries, Yamalo-Nenets National Okrug, Encyclopedia Arctica 10: Soviet North, Geography and General
sources.note: Digitized mid-twentieth-century unpublished typescript checked at scan and display pages 408 to 410 for Mangazeia knowledge, Russian sea travel, 1595 Dutch reports, and encounters with Nenets; pages 413 to 414 for tribute, exchange, and resistance. Its dated framing and OCR remain limitations.

sources.title: Words and Silences: Nenets Reindeer Herders and Russian Evangelical Missionaries in the Post-Soviet Arctic, Introduction
sources.note: Indiana University Press open book introduction checked in the subsection “The Nenets, Their Reindeer, and Their Others” for Pustozersk, tribute extraction, resistance, Obdorsk, and the much later chronology of large-scale mission work.

sources.title: Arctic Megapedia, Historical background of the Nenets
sources.note: Institutional Arctic reference checked in paragraphs 38 to 43 for the dated founding sequence of Pustozersk, Berezov, Surgut, Obdorsk, Mangazeya, and Turukhansk, trade, tribute, and resistance; its inherited Soviet-era framing is not adopted.

sources.title: Ural Federal University, Salekhard
sources.note: University regional-history page checked for the 1595 Obdorsk fort at an earlier Khanty settlement and the Nenets place-name Salekhard.

sources.title: Shiro Sasaki, Establishment of Large-Scale Reindeer Herding in European and West Siberian Tundra
sources.note: National Museum of Ethnology study checked at printed pages 79 to 80 for the proposed seventeenth- to nineteenth-century growth of large-scale herding and its especially later expansion.

sources.title: Kirill V. Istomin, Cultured reindeer, domesticated land, and (self)-cultivated herders: Histories and structures of reindeer herding landscapes in the European part of Russia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed article checked in the abstract and historical sections for small early-modern herds, transport, hunting, and later pastoral expansion in the European Russian and Archangelsk tundra scope.

sources.title: Røed et al., Temporal and structural genetic variation in reindeer associated with the pastoral transition in Northwestern Siberia
sources.note: Open peer-reviewed study checked in section 1, especially the paragraph beginning “The domestic reindeer studied,” for small domestic herds used in transport and hunting and the later pastoral transition.

sources.title: Kirill V. Istomin and Mark J. Dwyer, Reindeer Herders’ Thinking: A Comparative Research of Relations Between Economy, Cognition and Way of Life
sources.note: 2021 monograph checked at section 1.4, printed pages 25 to 26, for mobile hunting before later large-herd pastoralism.

sources.title: Irina Nikolaeva, A Grammar of Tundra Nenets
sources.note: Reference grammar checked at section 2.3, printed page 14 and PDF page 30, for the transcription system; and printed page 68, PDF page 84, example 25a for the exact modern sample, gloss, and translation. The copy is a university Moodle host; DOI 10.1515/9783110320640 secures publication identity.

sources.title: Josefina Budzisch, Beáta Wagner-Nagy, and Alexandre Arkhipov, INEL Nenets corpus: User documentation
sources.note: University corpus documentation checked at sections 1.1 to 1.2, pages 1 to 2; section 1.4, page 3; and sections 2.1 to 2.4, pages 5 to 6, for scope, lect distinctions, speakers, contributors, transcripts, glosses, and translations.

sources.title: Higher School of Economics, Грамматическое описание и документация лесного ненецкого языка (Grammatical Description and Documentation of the Forest Nenets Language)
sources.note: University project page checked at the purpose and resources sections for Pur Forest Nenets documentation, threatened status, lack of a literary norm, and planned grammar, texts, and dictionary outputs.

sources.title: Словарь (Forest Nenets Audio Dictionary)
sources.note: Project resource checked in the introduction, usage guide, and entry-structure description for searchable Forest Nenets headwords, Russian translations, usage examples, forms, and audio where available; used only as modern language work.

sources.title: Illinois State Museum, Hunters: Domestic Life
sources.note: Comparative Siberian museum exhibition checked for western Siberian chum construction, seasonal covers, sled transport, hide uses, and dated early twentieth-century photographs.

sources.title: Illinois State Museum, Hunters: Role of Reindeer
sources.note: Comparative Siberian museum exhibition checked for reindeer transport and material uses, with its regional breadth and twentieth-century photograph dates retained.

sources.title: Russian Ethnographic Museum, Malitsa with top piece, clothing for a male doll
sources.note: Museum catalog record checked for exact object identity, Nenets attribution, early twentieth-century date, reindeer-hide and cotton materials, dimensions, and collection context.

sources.title: Nenets Autonomous Okrug Museum, Toy cradle
sources.note: Regional museum page checked for the September 2008 toy cradle catalog record and, separately, the museum’s general text about full-size cradle suspension, seasonal covers, and sphagnum lining.

sources.title: Nenets Autonomous Okrug Museum, Uko doll
sources.note: Regional museum page checked for one Uko woman doll cataloged in 2005, NKM KP OF-3050, and separate interpretive prose explaining that such dolls can form families representing generations and support child learning.

sources.title: Security strategies of indigenous women in Nenets Autonomous Region, Russia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed article checked in methods and case sections for contemporary Nenets women, kin, care, household choices, paid and unpaid work, and regional specificity.

sources.title: Stephan Dudeck, Challenging the state educational system in Western Siberia: taiga school by the Tiuitiakha River
sources.note: University of Lapland research record checked in the abstract and publication metadata for a Forest Nenets family-organized taiga school, distant boarding-school pressures, its thirteen-year duration, and contemporary educational agency.

sources.title: Self-Identity Development among Indigenous Adolescents from the Far North of Russia
sources.note: Open peer-reviewed study checked in section 2.1, Participants, for 2018 Nenets respondents in the Nenets Autonomous District, boarding-school residence from September to May, and summer return to tundra families.

sources.title: Zoia Jefimovna Vylka Ravna, The Inter-Generational Transmission of Indigenous Knowledge by Nenets Women: Viewed in the Context of the State Educational System of Russia
sources.note: UiT doctoral thesis checked at PDF pages 3, 39, 43, 73, 148 to 150, and 220 for author position, fieldwork, observation, participation, play, language, chores, mobility, and explicit modern ethnographic limits.

sources.title: Effects of increase in temperature and open water on transmigration and access to health care by the Nenets reindeer herders in northern Russia
sources.note: Open peer-reviewed study checked in Methods and Results for modern Kanin migration, kin-based herding groups, seasonal access to health care, open-water barriers, and clinics.

sources.title: “Catching a Child”: giving birth under nomadic conditions. The methods of pre- and postnatal care of the Nenets mothers and babies
sources.note: Open peer-reviewed ethnography checked in methods and results for Nenets prenatal and postnatal care, women, infants, regional interviews, and the date limits of testimony.

sources.title: Our Neighbors: The Forest Nenets. Traditional Medicine
sources.note: Science First Hand museum-community article checked for jointly documented Forest Nenets remedies, named materials, field collection, and its modern project setting.

sources.title: Changing diets and traditional lifestyle of Siberian Arctic Indigenous Peoples and effects on health and well-being
sources.note: Open peer-reviewed Yamal-Nenets Autonomous Okrug study checked in background and dietary sections for present regional food patterns, health questions, and limits on historical inference.

sources.title: Traditional Living Habits of the Taz Tundra Population: A Paleoparasitological Study
sources.note: Open peer-reviewed archaeology study checked in site, methods, and discussion sections for historic Taz Nenets food, parasite evidence, and analytical limitations.

sources.title: The Yamal Nenets’ traditional and contemporary environmental knowledge of snow, ice, and permafrost
sources.note: Peer-reviewed open article checked in methods and results for Nenets snow, ice, water, route, camp, and shelter knowledge, including melting snow for drinking.

sources.title: Challenges of Changing Water Sources for Human Wellbeing in the Arctic Zone of Western Siberia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed open study checked in sections 3 and 5 and Table 3 for current Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug water sources, quality, infrastructure, and settlement-specific variation.

sources.title: Archived mirror of BBC - Tribe - Nenets
sources.note: Nonofficial archive mirror of the BBC companion checked in “Nenets life” for a contemporary Yamal camp, water carrying, and outdoor toilet areas away from chums and separated by gender; its localized observational scope is retained.

sources.title: Arctic Council, EALLU and Arctic Indigenous Peoples’ Food Systems
sources.note: Arctic Council page checked at paragraphs 3 to 17 for Indigenous-led food-knowledge work, youth, language, intergenerational workshops, and a contributor affiliated with the Centre for Reindeer Herding Development in Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug.

sources.title: Kautokeino Declaration: On the Occasion of the 4th World Reindeer Herders’ Congress
sources.note: Indigenous herder declaration checked at page 2 for women and knowledge transfer, pages 2 to 3 for family-based husbandry and local economy, and pages 3 to 5 for education, language, and youth.

sources.title: A. E. Nordenskiöld, The Voyage of the Vega Round Asia and Europe: With a Historical Review of Previous Journeys Along the North Coast of the Old World, volume I
sources.note: Public-domain volume checked at printed pages 100 to 101 for its transcription of Stephen Burrough’s 1556 report that Russian hunters told him of people called Samoeds; printed pages 222 to 224 separately describe the Kanin Nos route.

sources.title: Eszter Ruttkay-Miklián, Antal Reguly’s Data on the Ural Nenets
sources.note: Peer-reviewed article checked at PDF pages 8 to 11, journal pages 100 to 103, for sixteenth-century registration evidence and historical tundra and forest group distribution on both sides of the Urals.

sources.title: Yuri Kvashnin, To the Question of the South-Western Limits of Nomadic Nenets
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Herald of Anthropology 3 (2023) article checked at journal pages 52 to 67 for royal letters, petitions, travelers, westward routes, trade, exchange, conflict, and evidence limits.
